messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Bug in init/data parsing
parts:
Hey guys,

There appears to be a bug with how dump files are parsed when they're
passed as data or as init. I've attached a simple test case which
demonstrates the problem.

The model has a data matrix and a parameter matrix which have the same
dimension and are given the same data/initialization values. When run
the model produces the following:

$ ./datatest --point_estimate --iter=0 --data=datatest.data --init=datatest.data
STAN OPTIMIZATION COMMAND
data = datatest.data
init = datatest.data
output = samples.csv
save_warmup = 0
seed = 37934482 (randomly generated)
y_param = 1:0, y_data = 1
y_param = 3:0, y_data = 2
y_param = 5:0, y_data = 3
y_param = 2:0, y_data = 4
y_param = 4:0, y_data = 5
y_param = 6:0, y_data = 6
...

\It looks like the bug is in the handling of the inits as y_data is
parsed in column-major order as it shouild be but I haven't been able
to track it down.

Anyone willing to take a stab? I've run out of time and ideas for the day.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Bug in init/data parsing
parts:
Marcus, how the hell did you catch this??? Thanks for finding it.

Our writer (src/stan/io/writer.hpp) is pushing things in row-major, while our reader is pulling things out column-major. I'll add tests, fix it, and merge before our release tomorrow.



Daniel
